title: helianthemum origanifolium var. andalusicum
intro: Helianthemum origanifolium var. andalusicum, commonly known as Andalusian Rockrose, is a plant species native to the Iberian Peninsula. This shrubby perennial plant is known for its fragrant, pink or white flowers and its leaves, which have a strong, pungent aroma similar to oregano, hence its varietal name. The plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including digestive problems, fever, and respiratory issues, due to its therapeutic actions including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of Helianthemum origanifolium var. andalusicum include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
